what_round_11_claimed: 7 of 8 judges earned; earned set identical to the hand-typed set; 210 judgements across 30 real files with 0 disagreements
what_is_true: 5 exclusive + 2 nested, and the '0 disagreements' test could not have found the difference

the_defect.why_one_decoy_cannot_work: round 11 admitted a judge if it said 0 to a real file of the kind and non-zero to a single nonsense blob. That cannot distinguish 'rejects what is not my kind' from 'accepts my kind plus some other real kinds'

measured_cross_kind_matrix.gzip: exit 0 on a real ZIP FILE (gzip 1.12 prints 'OK') -- and 1 on the decoy, so round 11 admitted it
measured_cross_kind_matrix.tar: exit 0 on a real gzip stream
measured_cross_kind_matrix.python_ast: exit 0 on a real JSON document
measured_cross_kind_matrix.utf8_text: exit 0 on json, tar and python

the_defect.why_json_is_valid_python: `{"a": 1}` parses as a Python expression statement -- verified with ast.dump, so no parser-based judge can separate them
the_defect.consequence: a scan built on those judges would report a zip file as gzip -- the lying-name failure round 10 fixed, arriving through the validator instead of the suffix

the_fix.strict_test: a candidate must also REJECT every other real kind in the corpus, not just a nonsense decoy
the_fix.recovery: gzip and tar were recovered by ASKING A DIFFERENT QUESTION: `gzip -t` tests integrity and calls a zip OK, but reading a byte through the decompressor asks 'is this a gzip stream'. Same for tarfile.open vs tar -tf

the_second_correction.problem: the strict test is the right test for a kind and the wrong test for a NESTED kind
the_second_correction.measured: with the strict rule alone, 5 judges remain and 0% of /usr/share/doc and /usr/lib/python3 is readable -- because a .py file IS utf8 text and JSON IS parseable python
the_second_correction.fix: two admission classes. EXCLUSIVE must reject every other real kind. NESTED accepts a superset, which is CORRECT for a nested kind, and is admitted under a name saying it can never prove a file is NOT something else

an_api_trap_found_while_auditing.defect: Item.path is relative to the scan root, so signature(item.path, judges) resolves against the caller's cwd, finds nothing, returns ()
an_api_trap_found_while_auditing.measured: 0% of /usr/share/doc looked readable through that route while the same files read fine by absolute path -- every caller that re-judged what it was given would have reported every file unreadable
an_api_trap_found_while_auditing.fix: Item keeps the absolute path alongside the relative one, and rejudge() uses it

coverage_on_a_real_machine.elf: the largest unread class on a real machine. Four programs here judge it (readelf, objdump, nm, ldd) and all four agree; `readelf -h` was earned. `strings` was refused as a candidate in advance because it accepts everything

honest_limits: the candidate argv is still supplied by me; the loop decides WHETHER it is a judge, not which program to try
'exclusive' is a statement about the probe corpus, not a proof of exclusivity -- a kind not in the corpus could still be accepted
the nested class is declared per kind, so a genuinely nested kind not named in NESTED_KINDS is refused rather than classified
nested judges can only ever ADD a signature; they cannot make a file unreadable, but they also cannot distinguish structure
no benchmark task was run; this is a mechanism measurement
authority NONE, sandbox only, independent verification OPEN
the_next_bottleneck: choosing the candidate without me naming it -- and this round shows why that matters: every judge that survived was recovered by asking a DIFFERENT question of the same program, which is exactly what a named candidate list cannot do
